question:
A 21-year-old woman arrives at the emergency department 36 hours after a suspected sexual assault.
She recounts attending a party with a man she met online and believes she was drugged, as she only
consumed one alcoholic drink but has no memory of the evening until waking up partially undressed.
She reports vaginal pain and bruising but cannot recall what transpired. She is unsure if she has
completed the hepatitis B vaccination series. After conducting a full evaluation and discussing
postexposure prophylaxis for HIV, which combination of medications is most appropriate to offer this
patient? Answer Choices: (A) Azithromycin, ceftriaxone, hepatitis B vaccine, and mifepristone (B)
Azithromycin, ceftriaxone, metronidazole, hepatitis B immune globulin, and levonorgestrel (C)
Doxycycline, ceftriaxone, hepatitis B immune globulin, metronidazole, and levonorgestrel (D)
Doxycycline, ceftriaxone, hepatitis B immune globulin, and no emergency contraception (E)
Azithromycin, ceftriaxone, metronidazole, hepatitis B vaccine, and ulipristal acetate (F) Azithromycin,
ceftriaxone, metronidazole, hepatitis B vaccine, and no emergency contraception (G) Doxycycline,
ceftriaxone, metronidazole, hepatitis B vaccine, and levonorgestrel (H) Doxycycline, ceftriaxone,
levonorgestrel, and tetanus booster (I) Azithromycin, ceftriaxone, hepatitis B immune globulin, and
levonorgestrel (J) Doxycycline, ceftriaxone, metronidazole, hepatitis B vaccine, and mifepristone
 A. Doxycycline, ceftriaxone, hepatitis B immune globulin, and no emergency contraception
B. Doxycycline, ceftriaxone, hepatitis B immune globulin, metronidazole, and levonorgestrel
C. Doxycycline, ceftriaxone, metronidazole, hepatitis B vaccine, and mifepristone

D. Azithromycin, ceftriaxone, metronidazole, hepatitis B immune globulin, and levonorgestrel
E. Azithromycin, ceftriaxone, metronidazole, hepatitis B vaccine, and ulipristal acetate
F. Doxycycline, ceftriaxone, levonorgestrel, and tetanus booster
G. Azithromycin, ceftriaxone, hepatitis B vaccine, and mifepristone
H. Doxycycline, ceftriaxone, metronidazole, hepatitis B vaccine, and levonorgestrel
I. Azithromycin, ceftriaxone, hepatitis B immune globulin, and levonorgestrel
J. Azithromycin, ceftriaxone, metronidazole, hepatitis B vaccine, and no emergency contraception
